images.title: Faster speed, less time
images.purpose: Before and after: the same 100 km trip takes 2 hours at 50 km/h but only 1 h 20 min at 75 km/h, not 3 hours.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. Two equal road strips one above the other, each with one small motorcycle at its left end.
images.exact_structure: Two horizontal road strips of exactly the same length, one above the other, with one label 100 km centred between them under a double headed arrow spanning their length. Top strip in teal (#0072B2) with a small flat motorcycle icon at its left end, the label 50 km/h above the icon and 2 hours at the right end. Bottom strip in amber (#E69F00) with the same motorcycle icon, the label 75 km/h above the icon and 1 h 20 min at the right end. Next to 1 h 20 min, the text 3 hours in grey (#6B7280) with a single straight grey line through it. Nothing else in the frame, no rider, no scenery.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: When speed goes up, time goes down, so speed and time are not proportional.
images.description: Before and after: the same 100 km trip takes 2 hours at 50 km/h but only 1 h 20 min at 75 km/h, not 3 hours.
images.context: Distance 50 × 2 = 100 km; 100 ÷ 75 = 4/3 h = 1 h 20 min; Rule of Three would wrongly give 3 hours.
images.teaching_notes: 3 hours is struck out to show the wrong answer.

image_decisions.why: The equal road strips keep the distance fixed and show the time shrinking as speed grows.
